evidence:
Most of the 25 scored criteria are well separated, and many have explicit ownership notes: hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread say how quickly an update arrives is graded only in Functional; hro_pol_live_thread hands the scrolled-up case to hro_long_thread; hro_pol_failed_send hands note drafts to hro_pol_session_resume; hro_reject_reopen reads whether a reason is present only from current state, not Activity; hro_activity leaves out features that do not work and are graded elsewhere; hro_readonly_roles leaves out request kinds whose staff control failed; hro_intake_restart compares against the state recorded before the restart (lesson 16 baseline pattern). Role replays are separate (Observer, candidate and anonymous writes in hro_readonly_roles; manager rules in hro_manager_roles; conversation membership in hro_messaging; candidate reads in hro_candidate). I found no pair of criteria that requires incompatible products (409 for a stale move vs sending the current version in role replays; 403/404/401 split by session; Activity keeps the reason while card state drops it). Visual likert rows judge different aspects.
DEFECT 1 (two criteria grade the same observable): hro_messaging (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml, criterion at line 116, description ~line 121) step (2): 'Type a two-line message ... send with Enter ... reload and open the conversation again and read the box'. Its Bar says 'after the reload the sent text does not reappear'. hro_drafts (criterion at line 125, description ~line 130) says 'Send the first reply and read that box after a reload', and its Bar says 'after the first reply is sent its box stays empty after a reload'. Both check the same rule, hireops_rules.md:182 'Sending clears the draft.' -- that a sent message's saved draft is cleared and stays cleared after a reload. One defect therefore costs weight 4 + 2.
DEFECT 2 (lesson-16 pattern: a feature graded elsewhere decides another criterion's leg): hro_undo (line 80; Bar 'The undo is refused with nothing changed after another person ... re-ordered one within its stage (6), rejected one (7) and reopened a card Rafael rejected (8)'). This leg relies on Mei's re-order (graded in hro_moves), Mei's rejection and Mei's reopening (graded in hro_reject_reopen). functional/prompt.md:21 lets setup run against the state the app actually produced 'only to setup for a leg the Bar does not itself grade: every behaviour the Bar names (including any undo, re-order or move it lists) is graded here and is never left out'. That clause stops the judge from excusing these legs. So when the precondition feature fails, a correct undo, which goes ahead because nothing changed, fails hro_undo too. hro_bulk's Bar '(Y, W, X)' and hro_undo's '(Y, W, X, Z, A2)' quote orders that depend on step (2)'s re-order. They are partly softened by the actual-state rule, but the 'never left out' clause leaves this ambiguous.
Note (not counted as the Fail; it follows policy): if messages never arrive live, hro_messaging, hro_long_thread, hro_unread_seen and hro_pol_live_thread all lose credit. If board updates never arrive live, hro_two_people and hro_pol_live_board both lose credit. Each of these grades a distinct promise from hireops_rules.md section 5 (new messages, notice, unread counts, seen marks, preservation), and REVIEW_POLICY says a dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing. Likewise, missing undo zeroes hro_undo, hro_reject_reopen (undo of a reject/reopen, a distinct brief clause) and hro_interview_places (undo overfill, a distinct clause with its own goes-ahead control). These are accepted cascades, but the owner should know about them. No run was needed: this is a source-level check of how criteria relate.
counterexample: (a) Conforming app except for one defect: drafts are saved to localStorage on every keystroke, and Send clears the textarea but not the stored draft. After the reload, both hro_messaging (weight 4; every other leg passes) and hro_drafts (weight 2) fail for that one defect. (b) App whose up/down re-order request fails for a second recruiter (for example, it sends a stale position), but whose undo logic follows the rules exactly. hro_moves fails for the re-order defect, as it should. In hro_undo step (6), Mei's re-order does not happen, so Rafael's undo correctly goes ahead. The Bar requires a refusal, and prompt.md:21 forbids leaving the leg out, so hro_undo (weight 5) also fails. A rejection or reopening defect does the same through hro_undo steps (7) and (8).
suggested_fix: Remove the reload-after-send leg from hro_messaging (or mark it 'graded only in hro_drafts'). In hro_undo, judge legs (6)-(8) only when Mei's re-order/reject/reopen visibly succeeded (they are graded in hro_moves/hro_reject_reopen); otherwise leave the leg out and say why. Narrow the prompt.md:21 'never left out' clause to the criterion's own feature.
